scenario.zh: 排队时，有人直接插到你前面。你通常会怎么做？
scenario.en: You’re waiting in line and someone cuts right in front of you. What do you usually do?

text.zh: 直接指出来，让他回到队伍后面
text.en: Call it out and ask them to go to the back

interpretation.zh: 你可能认为规则值得被守护，哪怕需要自己开口。
interpretation.en: You may believe rules are worth defending — even when it takes speaking up yourself.

options.immediate: 用户似乎会当场登记并说出规则被打破这件事。

text.zh: 心里不舒服，但还是算了
text.en: It bothers me, but I let it go

interpretation.zh: 你似乎更愿意用忍让保全场面的平和——不舒服自己消化。
interpretation.en: You seem willing to swallow small discomforts to keep the peace — and digest them on your own.

options.immediate: 用户似乎感受到了不满，但选择绕开冲突、收住表达。

text.zh: 先看情况，影响比较大时才会说
text.en: Depends — I’d only say something if it really mattered

interpretation.zh: 你可能会先评估场合和分量，再决定要不要开口。
interpretation.en: You may size up the situation and the stakes before deciding to speak.

options.immediate: 用户似乎会先校准情境，把表达留给真正要紧的时刻。

text.en: Maybe they’re genuinely in a hurry

interpretation.zh: 你更倾向先替对方找一个善意的理由。
interpretation.en: You lean toward finding a kind reason for people first.

options.immediate: 用户似乎倾向于先做善意解读，并保留对人的判断。
